sentences.text: 1 (Per Hon'ble Sri Justice P.Naveen Rao)

This writ petition is filed praying to grant the following relief:
"...to issue an appropriate writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS under article 226 of Constitution of India declaring the order in C.No.551/WRC/CSB-XI/2021 dated 15.10.2021 of the respondents detaining the petitioner son namely Kandula Saitheja S/o Srinivas who is now detain in 3rd respondent prison before this Honble Court and he may order to be release forthwith after declaring his detention vide order in C.No.551/WRC/CSB-XI/2021 dated 15.10.2021 as illegal, unconstitutional and violation of the fundamental rights guaranteed under the constitution of India and pass..."

2. Heard Sri A. Jagan, learned counsel for petitioner and learned Government Pleader for Home,
appearing for respondents.
3.

This writ petition is filed by mother of the detenue, challenging the order of detention dated 15.10.2021, in exercise of the power under Section 3(2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and While Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act 1 of 1986).

entities.text: Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. The order of detention refers to four offences stated to have been committed by detenue on 12.04.2021.
These crimes were registered against detenue under Sections 395 and 394 respectively,
in Intezargunj
Police Station and Hasanparthy Police Station respectively.
5. It was alleged that detenue with three other co-accused resorted to dacoity on highways.

Such action of the detenue disturbs public order and if he was left scot-free, he would indulge in committing similar crimes affecting general public, causing fear and apprehension on people travelling on the road covering limits of these two police stations.
The order of detention was made after bail was granted by the competent Court.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the crimes registered against detenue were ordinary crimes which could be prosecuted under criminal procedure code and do not require taking recourse to preventive detention.
7. It is appropriate to note that the detenue was not involved in any other crimes of similar nature earlier and all the four crimes were stated to have been occurred on the very same day.
8. The learned counsel for the petitioner places reliance on the decision of this Court in W.P.No.9334 of 2021.
In the said case, detenue was treated as a 'Goonda' as he was alleged to have been involved in robbery at Singareni Collieries Company Limited in the limits of Ramagundam Police Commissionerate.
During the period from 2010 to 2020, he was involved in 27 offences.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Holding that on the crimes alleged against the detenue, preventive detention was not warranted,
this Court allowed the writ petition.

9. In the instant case also, by involving in these four crimes it cannot be said that detenue has created a panic situation and fear in people travelling on roads in those areas, to resort to the extra ordinary measure of preventively detaining him.
The Court is also informed that though 4 people were stated to have been involved in committing crime, only the detenue was detained and other three were not detained.
10. We are of the opinion that in the facts of this case, the detention under the Act 1 of 1986, was not warranted.
11. Though learned Government Pleader sought to contend that there was slight difference between the said case and the case on hand, we do not appreciate the said contention.
We are in agreement with the view taken by the Division Bench of this Court in W.P.No.9334 of 2021.
12. In the result, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order passed by the Office of the Commissioner of Police, Warangal, Warangal District- 2nd respondent vide C.No.551/WRC/CSB-XI/2021 dated 15.10.2021 and the consequential confirmation order of the Principal Secretary to Government, Hyderabad, approving the detention vide G.O.Rt.No.2890,
General Administration (SPL. (Law & Order) Department dated 28.12.2021, are hereby set aside.

The respondents are directed to set the detenu, namely Kandula Saitheja, S/o. Srinivas, aged about 26 years, Caste:
Munnurukapu, R/o. H.No. 17-2-396, Beerannakunta, Ursu Kareemabad, Warangal,
at liberty forthwith, if he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
Miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.

P. NAVEEN RAO, J ________________________ DR. G. RADHA RANI, J 16th February, 2022 PT THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE P.
